data.name: Cli_Usage
data.value:
hexbridge-receiver — a microphone bridge between two machines. It does both ends: receives somebody else's microphone, and shares its own.
Usage: hexbridge-receiver [flags] run in the role from the config (receiving by default) hexbridge-receiver list-devices list output devices and the microphones they pair with hexbridge-receiver list-inputs list this machine's microphones hexbridge-receiver keygen generate a pairing key (PSK)
Both roles: --config PATH path to the config (config.json next to the exe by default) --role ROLE receiver — take somebody else's microphone, sender — share this one --psk BASE64 pairing key, 32 bytes of base64; the same on both machines --relay H:P go through a relay instead of connecting directly --quiet do not print the statistics line every 5 seconds
When this computer receives a microphone: --listen [A:]P what to listen on (0.0.0.0:47702 by default) --device SEL part of the output device name; detected automatically by default --jitter MS target buffer depth, ms (60 by default) --max-jitter MS the buffer is trimmed above this (240 by default) --gain F output gain, 1.0 leaves it alone --latency MS WASAPI latency to ask for (50 by default) --output MODE wasapi (default), null, or wav:path — for diagnostics --no-gamepad no USB forwarding, sound only --usbip PATH path to usbip.exe, if it is not in C:\Program Files\USBip
When this computer shares its microphone: --target H:P address of the other machine; required unless --relay is set --input MODE wasapi (default), null, tone, or wav:path --input-device S part of the microphone name; the system default otherwise --input-gain F input gain, 1.0 leaves it alone --bitrate BPS Opus bitrate (32000 by default) --muted start with the microphone muted
